key_insight: MindView tests whether AI can generate spatially consistent views of a scene from partial multi-view observations and language instructions. It introduces a benchmark with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets.
problem_solved: Existing generative spatial evaluations leave language-guided view generation underexplored: can a model infer a scene’s spatial structure and depict it consistently from a requested viewpoint?
method: Combine partial multi-view scene observations with language instructions to evaluate spatially consistent image generation.
Organize seven tasks into two families, including geometry-dominant tasks that specify changes in camera position and orientation.
Use 1,500 samples covering 513 scenes from three indoor datasets. The provided abstract is truncated, so the second task family and evaluation details are unavailable.
impact: MindView gives practitioners a benchmark for testing spatial reasoning through generated views, beyond image editing alone. It can help assess whether visual plausibility is supported by consistent scene geometry.
